title: A closed subscheme is an effective Cartier divisor if and only if it is locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor

standard_prerequisites.name: Effective Cartier divisors via the ideal sheaf: a closed subscheme D of a scheme S with ideal sheaf I_D is an effective Cartier divisor exactly when I_D is an invertible O_S-module, and on the open complement S minus D the restriction of I_D is O
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Supplies both directions of the equivalence used and concluded at proof lines 2415-2418 and 2430-2432
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the target of the second direction and the starting point of the first: invertibility of I_D is what has to be translated into the local equation f.

standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-coherence of ideal sheaves and the tilde construction over an affine open Spec(A): sections of I_D over U correspond to an ideal of A, and D cap U = Spec(A/(f)) when the restriction of I_D is generated by f
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Used at proof lines 2418-2421 and again at 2426-2429
standard_prerequisites.use: Converts the chosen free generator f of the sections of I_D into an element of A and identifies the closed subscheme it cuts out.

core_obligations: From (1) to (2): at a point x of D choose an affine open U = Spec(A) around x with I_D restricted to U isomorphic to O_U, and choose a section f of I_D over U which freely generates that restriction (proof lines 2415-2419).
Read f as an element of A, observe that multiplication by f on A is injective because f is a nonzerodivisor, and use quasi-coherence of I_D to conclude D cap U = Spec(A/(f)) (proof lines 2419-2421).

From (2) to (1): over an affine open U = Spec(A) with U cap D = Spec(A/(f)) and f a nonzerodivisor, show I_D restricted to U is isomorphic to O_U by identifying it with the tilde of the principal ideal (f) (proof lines 2423-2429).

Finish invertibility: I_D restricted to the open complement of D is isomorphic to O, so I_D is an invertible O_S-module, which is the definition of an effective Cartier divisor (proof lines 2430-2432).
proof_roadmap: Direction (1) to (2): invertibility of I_D over an affine open yields a free generator f, whose nonzerodivisor property makes A to A injective and identifies D locally with Spec(A/(f)) (proof lines 2415-2421).
Direction (2) to (1): a local equation f produces an isomorphism I_D to O over the affine open and over the complement of D, giving invertibility of I_D (proof lines 2423-2432).
difficulty_reason: The statement is the standard local characterization of effective Cartier divisors: for a closed subscheme D of a scheme S, being locally cut out by a single nonzerodivisor is equivalent to the ideal sheaf I_D being invertible (statement lines 2402-2413). The proof is short but runs both directions of the equivalence and needs the dictionary between an invertible ideal sheaf, a free generator f of its sections over an affine open, and the closed subscheme Spec(A/(f)); the passage from I_D restricted to U being O_U to the injectivity of multiplication by f, and the use of quasi-coherence of I_D to identify D cap U, are the non-formal moves (proof lines 2416-2421 and 2426-2432). It is H2: no hypothesis on S beyond being a scheme is used and the argument is a local computation, but no step is replaced by a citation.
